name: Dalea

project_scope.selection_mode: twelve-canonical-comparison, range status per original species
project_scope.note: 12 distinct already installed canonical Dalea learner cards. This genus lesson broadens the original B010/B068 4+1 comparison but changes no species admission, scientific county-range status, or taxonomy. Some species have only external images or none; never count linked-only photos as installed.

shared_traits: small flowers arranged in spikes or headlike clusters
study_strategy.warning: Do not identify Dalea from flower color alone. D. compacta vs D. purpurea especially requires calyx-level confirmation.

quick_key.if: Stiff, many-branched WOODY SHRUB with many small pinnate leaflets, short flower spikes
quick_key.then: D. frutescens; compare woody D. greggii if low/trailing

quick_key.if: Spreading, low grayish-silky subshrub, rooting or hugging ground, with small purple flowers
Few larger silky leaflets, remarkably hairy FUZZY golden/white terminal head
quick_key.then: D. aurea (look at hair texture rather than only yellow tone)

quick_key.if: Mostly white petals, tall narrow cylindrical densely flowered spike, gland-dotted narrow leaflets
quick_key.then: D. candida (project range UNRESOLVED); verify against compact D. multiflora

quick_key.if: Long, THIN elongated spike with individual flowers and broad bracts spaced apart
quick_key.then: D. enneandra; use calyx/stamen macro to confirm

quick_key.if: Dense purple/pink cylindrical/ovoid spike and fine narrow leaves
quick_key.then: D. compacta versus D. purpurea: examine calyx TUBE hair relative to calyx TEETH

quick_key.if: Tiny plant with short ovoid head and possible mixed yellow/pink-to-purple old flowers
Small round pink-purple head, mostly THREE extremely slender linear leaflets
quick_key.then: D. tenuis (linked-only photo in current learner; macro to confirm)

quick_key.if: Low many-stemmed plant with small WHITE round clusters and about three tiny leaflets
quick_key.then: D. multiflora; watch for overlap with D. candida

quick_key.if: Slender perennial with mostly 3 leaflets and loosely arranged yellow flowers
Downy dry-country herb and purple-violet spikes but incomplete proven structural views
quick_key.then: D. neomexicana: learner UNRESOLVED, photo missing; do not force an ID

b068_study_strategy.warning: Several Dalea are widely sold or broadly Texas-native. Keep exact-county native evidence separate from horticultural occurrence.

quick_split: D. hallii — slender perennial, usually 3-foliolate, loose yellow flower spikes; local PASS.
D. candida — dense white cylindrical spikes and several narrow leaflets; range HOLD.
D. greggii — low spreading gray subshrub with tiny silky leaflets and purple flowers; western range HOLD.
D. neomexicana — downy perennial dry-country prairie clover with purple-violet spikes; western range HOLD.
D. purpurea — existing purple prairie clover anchor.

look_here_first: FIRST study plant habit: woody shrub versus herb versus low spreading mat. SECOND examine a FULL pinnate leaf—count complete LEAFLETS (the individual small blades) and check width, silvery hairs, and translucent GLAND DOTS. THIRD inspect one whole FLOWER SPIKE/HEAD: tight fuzzy oval/cylinder or long loose axis with flowers spaced apart. FOURTH zoom into a single floral CALYX: its teeth and tiny gland/hair placement separate notoriously similar purple heads (e.g. D. compacta vs D. purpurea). The fruit is a very small LEGUME mostly enclosed by the persistent calyx; a tiny seed-bearing pod does NOT look like a mesquite pod.
shared_traits: Most project Dalea have alternate pinnately compound leaves, often with visible gland dots and small leaflets; some are erect herbs and some are woody subshrubs.
Dense or elongated flower SPIKES/HEADS contain MANY tiny individual flowers; the hairy or bract-covered cone is an INFLORESCENCE, not one entire flower.

Each flower has a little tubular CALYX with five teeth; the petal and stamen arrangement is modified from the familiar banner, wings and keel legume flower plan. Do not infer exact petal positions without a close flower macro.
The fruit is a tiny one- or few-seeded LEGUME, often enclosed within the persistent calyx. A small dry pod still places it in Fabaceae.
Flower color ranges from white to yellow to purple, sometimes changing with age; do not use color as a species ID key.

genus_diagnostics.habit: First compare the WHOLE PLANT. D. frutescens is a many-branched woody shrub; D. greggii is a spreading low woody/semishrub, while D. aurea, candida, compacta, purpurea, hallii etc. are more upright herbs. Habit overlaps or can be altered by grazing, so never stop here.
genus_diagnostics.leaves: Examine a COMPLETE pinnately compound leaf: leaflets are the individual blades. Number, length/width, hairiness and gland dots are the next clues. D. aurea often has relatively few larger silky leaflets; D. purpurea and D. compacta commonly have several narrow almost linear leaflets; D. hallii/tenuis/multiflora often mostly three.
genus_diagnostics.inflorescence: Spikes can be tightly cylindrical/conical or loosely flowered. D. enneandra has a conspicuously slender elongated loose spike. D. compacta, purpurea and candida have tight dense heads/spikes. Some flowers open sequentially from base up; one head contains many florets, not one bloom.
genus_diagnostics.calyx: The persistent CALYX (fused sepals) forms a tiny tube bearing teeth. D. compacta versus D. purpurea: per Flora of North Central Texas, compacta calyx tube is largely glabrous while teeth hairy; purpurea tube and teeth densely hairy. Distinguish a bare CALYX TUBE from a bract/hair: only a matching real magnified single flower can verify this. Other local species differ in teeth, gland dots and hair direction.
genus_diagnostics.flower: Many small pea-family flowers with specialized, modified banner/wings/keel and a usually small stamen column. Flower color changes/overlaps and a fluffy spike does not prove same species. D. enneandra is named for its generally nine stamens; a true dissection is needed before claiming to COUNT stamens in a photograph.
genus_diagnostics.fruit: The tiny mature indehiscent or weakly opening LEGUME can be held inside persistent sepals, not a long pod like a bean. Specialized ripe pod plus calyx macro is needed; the existing head/habit gallery is insufficient to prove fruit and seed anatomy.
genus_diagnostics.glands: Look at LEAFLET undersides and sepals/bracts for tiny dark or translucent GLAND DOTS, often oil-resin glands. They can look like tiny punctations, and must be resolved in a macro before placing a verified arrow.
genus_diagnostics.stem: Woody branch versus annual herbaceous shoot strongly directs you to the right subgroup, but distinguish shoot from leaf stalk and leaf rachis; do not confuse a single leaflet with the whole pinnate leaf.

comparison_cards.title: Compact versus purple prairie clover
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Color and flower-head silhouette overlap. Inspect a single side-on CALYX tube: D. compacta calyx tube largely bare but teeth hairy; D. purpurea tube densely hairy as well as teeth. Match focus/scale, see the actual calyx, not just head bracts.
photo_requirements: same-scale extracted single calyx, D. compacta vs D. purpurea, showing tube and tooth pubescence
whole head side views and full pinnate leaf
comparison_cards.caution: The two existing primary head views are not diagnostic calyx macros; rights-unverified purpurea image for private study only.

comparison_cards.title: White prairie clover versus small white daleas
comparison_cards.look_here_first: CANDIDA often has a tall dense cylindrical white spike with multiple leaflets; MULTIFLORA has smaller more globose white heads on a lower, fine-textured, often mostly 3-foliolate plant. Compare a WHOLE STEM and full leaf before one close spike.
photo_requirements: whole height/habit and true leaf leaflet count at same scale
close bract and calyx gland macro
comparison_cards.caution: The D. multiflora study photo is CC BY-NC and not cleared for commercial/public reuse.

comparison_cards.title: Golden prairie clovers
comparison_cards.look_here_first: AUREA has very conspicuously silky leaflets and dense fuzzy heads. HALLII is slender, often 3-leafleted and has relatively loose yellow-flowered spikes. Compare hair and spike density, not yellow flower color alone.
photo_requirements: full leaves and whole bloom axes, head/hair macro
public-cleared physical gallery for hallii (currently external references)

comparison_cards.title: Black dalea versus spreading Gregg's dalea
comparison_cards.look_here_first: Frutescens forms an intricately branched upright woody shrub. Greggii grows low/trailing and can root where stems contact ground. Individual tiny leaflets and floral features still matter.
photo_requirements: whole plants and close woody joints/rooting nodes
comparison_cards.caution: Current Greggs source is a photographed cultivated specimen, NOT county-native proof.

visual_comparison.title: Dalea: twelve prairie-clover names, multiple real photo doors
visual_comparison.subtitle: Ten physically installed study images illustrating eight species, labeled separately from the four genus species currently relying only on external photo references or no local image. Structure-first key: habit → leaflets → spike → calyx → pod.
visual_comparison.memory_rule: WOODY shrub (frutescens) vs SPRAWLING gray mat (greggii) vs upright herb. DENSE fuzzy aurea vs DENSE white candida/multiflora vs LOOSE enneandra. Two common purple heads (compacta/purpurea) need CALYX-TUBE hairs, not color.

items.label: Golden prairie clover: silky, fuzzy flower head
items.creator: Source photographer not recorded in canonical metadata
items.caption: Look at the shaggy whitish/silky hairs covering the tightly packed head. Golden flower color alone is not the diagnostic; the few relatively large silky leaflets and cone-like fuzzy head are useful in combination.

items.label: White prairie clover: cylindrical flower spike
items.creator: Jasper Shide
items.caption: Follow the white blooms upward from the lower part of the cone-shaped/cylindrical spike. A SPIKE is made of many separate tiny flowers, not a single big flower. Petal positions and glands will require a true flower macro.

items.label: Compact prairie clover: dense swollen head
items.creator: Source photographer not recorded in canonical metadata
items.caption: Find the swollen compact flower head first. This species and purple prairie clover can overlap greatly in color and head shape; the key distinction is hairy CALYX tube versus its teeth, neither confirmed from this overall head photo.

items.label: Black dalea: woody shrub habit
items.image_role: many-branched woody shrub and small foliage
items.creator: Source photographer not recorded in canonical metadata
items.caption: Follow the stiff perennial woody branches and tiny divided leaves. A sprawling woody plant moves you toward black dalea and other shrubby Dalea, not upright herbaceous prairie clover; flowers and leaflets still need a close-up.

items.label: Gregg's dalea: low, spreading foliage
items.creator: Stan Shebs
items.caption: Examine the spreading, low growth and small gray-green silky leaflets around purple flowers. The original photograph is of a cultivated specimen; it is a morphology reference, NOT a Texas-range voucher.

items.label: Manyflower prairie clover: small white head
items.image_role: compact pale flower head on low plant
items.creator: Judith Lopez Sikora
items.caption: Small whitish flower heads and low stems are part of a suite including 3 slender leaflets and gland-dotted foliage. This one existing photo is noncommercial study media; its fine glands are not visually resolved. This source is FOR PRIVATE STUDY / RIGHTS REVIEW ONLY; do not use for public promotion.

items.label: Dwarf dalea: tiny mixed-color flower spike
items.image_role: small globular spike and silky foliage
items.creator: Frankie Coburn
items.caption: Look for a low tufted plant and a short oval head. Flowers may shift from yellow to pink-purple with age; mixing colors on one head can happen and should not be treated as two species.

items.label: Purple prairie clover: densely packed flower head
items.image_role: purple flower head / narrow leaflet context
items.creator: R.W. Smith
items.caption: Compare this purple head with D. compacta. FNA/Flora of North Central Texas keys distinguish the outside of the CALYX: purpurea = tube and teeth both hairy; compacta = tube largely bare while teeth remain hairy. The hair placement requires a sharp side macro, not just this portrait. This source is FOR PRIVATE STUDY / RIGHTS REVIEW ONLY; do not use for public promotion.

items.label: Purple prairie clover: whole plant habit
items.creator: W.D. and Dolphia Bransford
items.caption: Find the slender upright stems, few fine leaflets and terminal flower heads. This scene is a habit comparison, not an audited calyx-teeth photograph; rights must be reviewed before public distribution. This source is FOR PRIVATE STUDY / RIGHTS REVIEW ONLY; do not use for public promotion.
